guarantee.conservatism: A competitor tying the true winner need not become the global empirical winner, so the radius is safe but can be smaller than the exact bad-winner-region distance.
guarantee.event: empirical winner true regret <= declared tolerance
guarantee.radius: minimum pairwise L1 distance to an unacceptable competitor tying the true winner

overestimate_radius_2.description: Non-exact mass is split equally between one- and two-cell overestimation.

symmetric_radius_1.description: Non-exact mass is split equally between adjacent lower and higher cost cells.

symmetric_radius_2.description: Non-exact mass is split equally across one- and two-cell errors in either direction.

underestimate_radius_2.description: Non-exact mass is split equally between one- and two-cell underestimation.

limitations: The pairwise-safe radius is conservative because an unacceptable competitor can tie the true winner without becoming the global empirical winner.
Regret tolerances are absolute regression fractions, not utility-, latency-, or SLO-weighted deployment costs.
The multinomial concentration bound is distribution-free and conservative; exact confidence regions can require fewer samples.
The 10% prevalence simplex and E88 sensitivity kernels are not calibrated deployment distributions.
The audit reuses compact E83 path summaries and is not new GPU evidence.
model: Select a policy from empirical six-cell prevalence while guaranteeing that its true weighted regression is within a declared absolute tolerance of the true prevalence winner. The pairwise-safe radius is the exact minimum L1 distance at which any policy whose true regret exceeds the tolerance can tie the true winner.
